sections.title: Message from the Provincial Superior
sections.markdown:
## A message of gratitude during Jubilee 2025

**Sr. Pauline Nusi, JMJ — Provincial Superior, Hyderabad Province (as identified in the January–March 2025 Jubilee Vibes issue).**

In her foreword to the first *Jubilee Vibes* booklet, Sr. Pauline invited the Sisters and the wider JMJ family to remember the grace-filled experiences of the Jubilee Year with gratitude. She presented the booklet as a space for Sisters' reflections, personal testimonies, stories of faith and service, and photographs of shared celebrations.

She encouraged communities to read and discuss the contributions together and to let these memories renew their commitment to their vocation, to one another, and to the mission of love and service entrusted to JMJ. The invitation is especially meaningful in a Jubilee year: to celebrate what God has done and to carry its inspiration into everyday community and apostolic life.

## Read the Provincial Superior's original foreword

The text above is a **summary of the foreword in Jubilee Vibes, Issue 1 (January–March 2025)**. It is not presented as a new 2026 pastoral letter.

- [Open Jubilee Vibes 1 — the foreword appears in the booklet](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1HV6P8ENNQ8nS2LtSjQik_3R9ZR04Pba2/view).
- [Explore all Jubilee Vibes issues](/news-flash/jubilee-vibes).

For an updated personal message from the Provincial Superior, please [contact the Hyderabad Provincialate](/contact).

sections.title: Provincial Chapter 2023
sections.markdown:
## Synodal Solidarity towards Universal Fraternity

The JMJ Hyderabad Province held its Provincial Chapter in **two phases: 21–24 August 2023 and 10–14 October 2023**. The Chapter's theme called the delegates to discern the Province's future together in a spirit of fraternity, attentive listening, prayer, and shared responsibility.

## Preparation in local communities

The preparatory Local Chapter took place **2 February–30 April 2023**. Sisters reflected on *Fratelli Tutti*, synodality, their Constitutions, the Founder's spirituality and charism, and the challenges confronting their communities and ministries. Prayer, faith-sharing and reflection helped delegates prepare for the Provincial Chapter.

## Phase I — 21–24 August 2023

Delegates examined reports from the Province and its different apostolates, considered survey findings and postulates, and discerned possible priorities and action plans. The process encouraged an honest review of the Province's strengths, difficulties and opportunities for renewed mission.

## Phase II — 10–14 October 2023

The delegates considered proposals for the **2024 General Chapter**, discussed suggested changes to the Constitutions and norms, elected delegates for the General Chapter, and planned further post-Chapter work. Across both phases, spiritual reflection accompanied practical discussion and decision-making.

## Continuing the journey

The Chapter's reflections emphasized renewal of JMJ identity, stronger collaboration, attention to people at the margins, and the Congregation's charism of ever-adaptable apostolic availability. Its implementation belongs to the subsequent work of the Province's communities and apostolates.

**Source:** [*The Encounter*, December 2023 — account of the Hyderabad Provincial Chapter](https://cjmjbangaloreprovince.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/The-Encounter-December-2023.pdf). This is a summary of the published account, not a reproduction of official Chapter minutes.

sections.title: JMJ Subodha Centre
sections.markdown:
**Pastoral Care and Evangelization – Hyderabad Province**

## Our Mission: Proclaiming Christ with Faith, Hope and Joy

> “Let us witness to the newness, hope, and joy that the Lord brings to life. Let us feel within us ‘the delightful and comforting joy of evangelizing’ (Evangelii Nuntiandi, 80). Because evangelizing, proclaiming Jesus, gives us joy. Instead, egoism makes us bitter, sad and depresses us. Evangelizing uplifts us.”
>
> — Pope Francis

## Our Call to Evangelization

By virtue of our sacred vocation, Jesus lovingly calls us to Himself, consecrates us, and sends us into the world to proclaim His Good News. Therefore, evangelization is at the heart of our religious life and mission. It is the responsibility of every JMJ Sister, every community, and every apostolate.

Pastoral care and evangelization are inseparably connected. Evangelization is an essential dimension of pastoral care, and every pastoral activity is an opportunity to lead people to a deeper encounter with Christ. Inspired by the missionary mandate of Jesus, we continue to embrace His call:

> “Go therefore and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit… And remember, I am with you always, to the end of the age.” (Matthew 28:19–20)

## Our Missionary Heritage

Our Dutch pioneers, who arrived in India more than a century ago, began this ministry through lives of sacrifice, dedication, prayer, and personal witness. In collaboration with bishops and priests, they generously participated in pastoral and catechetical activities in the local Church.

They regularly visited Christian and non-Christian families in distant villages and urban communities. Often staying overnight in villages, they adapted themselves to unfamiliar cultures, languages, food, accommodation, travel difficulties, and climatic conditions. Their loving presence became a blessing to the people. They were welcomed as mothers who genuinely cared for the people, shared their struggles, and accompanied them through their joys and difficulties.

Through their committed service, Christian communities grew, and new sub-parishes developed around established centres. Our educational institutions and healthcare apostolates have also become places where Christian values are expressed through compassionate care, selfless service, and dedication to human dignity. Alongside these services, catechetical instruction and pastoral accompaniment continue to nurture faith and bring people closer to Christ.

## The Vision of Our Founder

The missionary mandate of Jesus was embraced and lived with conviction by our Venerable Founder, Rev. Fr. Mathias Wolff SJ, and passed on through generations of JMJ Sisters. His missionary spirit continues to inspire us to proclaim the Gospel through our lives and ministries.

For many JMJ Sisters, the desire to participate in catechetical instruction, pastoral care, and evangelization has been a significant inspiration for embracing religious life. Our missionary heritage reminds us that education, healthcare, and every other apostolate find their deepest meaning in witnessing to Christ and serving His people with love.

Even in the Netherlands, pastoral care preceded the educational apostolate, revealing the foundational importance of accompanying people in their faith journey.

## JMJ Subodha Centre: Awakening, Accompanying and Empowering

JMJ Subodha Centre, Kurnool-3, Andhra Pradesh, under Pastoral and Evangelization of the Hyderabad Province, is a centre of faith formation, missionary animation, and pastoral renewal. It seeks to strengthen the evangelizing mission of the JMJ Congregation by equipping sisters and collaborating with the local Church to respond to the spiritual and pastoral needs of people today.

The Centre envisions evangelization not merely as the proclamation of the Gospel in words, but as a way of life rooted in prayer, compassionate presence, joyful witness, and loving service. It seeks to build bridges between faith and everyday life, helping individuals and communities encounter Christ personally and grow as committed witnesses to the Gospel.

## Our Areas of Mission

Through its pastoral and evangelizing initiatives, JMJ Subodha Centre promotes:

- **Faith Formation and Catechesis:** Deepening knowledge of Scripture, Church teachings, prayer, and Christian living.
- **Youth and Children's Ministry:** Accompanying young people and children in their faith journey and encouraging them to become joyful witnesses of Christ.
- **Family Ministry:** Strengthening families as domestic churches rooted in faith, love, prayer, and mutual care.
- **Lay Collaboration:** Encouraging laypeople to share their gifts and actively participate in the mission of the Church.
- **Community Outreach:** Reaching out to families, the poor, the marginalized, and those in need through compassionate pastoral presence.
- **Digital Evangelization:** Using digital platforms creatively and responsibly to proclaim Christ and communicate the Gospel message.
- **Missionary Animation:** Inspiring JMJ Sisters and communities to renew their missionary commitment and respond to the changing needs of the Church and society.

## Our Commitment

JMJ Subodha Centre strives to foster a living, vibrant, and missionary Church in which every person experiences the love of Christ and discovers the joy of the Gospel. Through formation programmes, pastoral initiatives, youth and family ministry, community outreach, and collaboration with the local Church, the Centre seeks to awaken faith, accompany people in their struggles, and empower them to become missionary disciples.

Inspired by the missionary zeal of our Founder and the selfless witness of our pioneers, we continue to respond to the call of Jesus with renewed enthusiasm and dedication.

Our conviction is simple: **evangelization is not merely what we do; it is who we are as followers of Christ and members of the JMJ Congregation.**

May JMJ Subodha Centre continue to be a beacon of faith, hope, and joy, proclaiming Christ with creativity, compassion, and communion, and bringing the Good News to every heart and every home.

sections.title: JMJ Spirituality & Charism
sections.markdown:
Our way of life grows out of the Ignatian spirituality of our Founder, **Rev. Fr. Mathias Wolff S.J.**, a Jesuit priest whose one desire was to do the will of God. Seeking that will, again and again, makes discernment part of every Sister's daily life.

## An interior and an exterior spirit

The Founder asked his Sisters to unite two things in one life.

### The interior spirit
A JMJ Sister is to be possessed by God from within, so that all her outward work is done for His greater glory. This shows itself in:

- self-denial and a true sense of what earthly things are worth;
- a growing knowledge of the things of God and joy in Him;
- faithfulness to prayer and trust in the Holy Spirit;
- inner freedom and zeal for God's honour.

### The exterior spirit
Outwardly she lives a simple, ordinary life among the people she serves, giving herself to her work with apostolic courage and love of neighbour. She is marked by obedience, modesty, recollection, prudence in speech, and a readiness to serve without seeking attention.

## Our charism: An Ever-Adaptable Apostolic Availability

A charism is a gift of the Holy Spirit that makes a person especially sensitive to one aspect of the mystery of Christ. Our Founder's own gift was a burning readiness for souls and a willingness to labour without tiring — a gift he handed on to the Society he founded.

The Congregation names this charism **"An Ever-Adaptable Apostolic Availability."** Each Sister is invited to read the signs of the times and respond with courage, as the Founder did, always listening to the Holy Spirit and to the will of God.

## The Founder's three instructions (1827)

1. **A religious spirit** — the aim is to form true religious, not only devout Christian women.
2. **A spirit of obedience** — readiness to go wherever one is sent.
3. **Intimacy with God** — meditation comes first; other prayers and reading may give way to it when needed.

Related pages: [Our Founder](/who-we-are/founder) · [Vision & Mission Statement](/who-we-are/vision-mission) · [Our Life With God](/spirituality/life-with-god)

---

*Adapted from the Congregation of Jesus Mary Joseph website: [https://congregationjmj.org/jmj-spirituality-charism](https://congregationjmj.org/jmj-spirituality-charism).*

sections.title: Our Life With God
sections.markdown:
Prayer is the heart of our consecrated life. In prayer each Sister is drawn more deeply into the love of Christ and the mystery of His death and resurrection, and from prayer she goes out to serve.

## Contemplation in action

Our Founder wished each Sister to be "interiorly possessed by God". We live this as *contemplation in action*: a close, personal friendship with God that shapes everything we do. For this reason every Sister gives at least **one hour each day to personal prayer**, listening to God in her heart.

## Prayer and mission go together

Prayer is both the foundation of our life and the driving force of our mission. Seeking God above all things, we see ourselves as His co-workers in the work of redemption and in building His Kingdom. Prayer shapes our apostolate, and the apostolate leads us back to prayer.

## Prayer in community

Each community is nourished by silence, by personal and shared prayer, by the sacraments and by sharing our faith with one another. We try to keep a healthy balance between work and rest, recreation and silence, conversation and recollection.

## Our daily and yearly practices

- **Personal prayer** — one hour every day
- **The Word of God** — meditation on Scripture and spiritual reading
- **Holy Eucharist** — daily Mass and Eucharistic adoration
- **Reconciliation** — regular celebration of the sacrament
- **Examen** — a daily examination of conscience
- **Liturgy of the Hours** — prayed together in community
- **Devotions** — to the Holy Family, Jesus, Mary and Joseph, our patrons; to the Sacred Heart of Jesus and the Immaculate Heart of Mary
- **Formation reading** — the documents of the Congregation and the writings of our Founder
- **Retreat and recollection** — an eight-day Ignatian retreat each year and a day of recollection each month
- **Spiritual direction**

Related pages: [JMJ Spirituality & Charism](/spirituality/charism) · [Prayers of the Congregation](/spirituality/prayers) · [Our Life in the Community](/who-we-are/our-life)

---

*Adapted from the Congregation of Jesus Mary Joseph website: [https://congregationjmj.org/our-life-with-god](https://congregationjmj.org/our-life-with-god).*

sections.title: Prayers of the Congregation
sections.markdown:
These are the prayers that unite the Sisters of Jesus Mary Joseph across our communities in India, Africa, Europe and the Americas. The full texts are kept on the Congregation's website.

## Prayer to Jesus Mary Joseph

We place ourselves under the patronage of the Holy Family — Jesus, Mary and Joseph, the patrons of our Congregation — asking their blessing on every Sister, the grace to live our calling faithfully, good and genuine vocations, and the growth of God's Kingdom.

## Prayer of Fr. Mathias Wolff S.J.

A short prayer of our Founder, asking God to change our hearts and to let us find our happiness in doing His will.

## Prayer for the Beatification of our Founder

We ask God that, if it is His will, the Church may one day honour our Founder, Rev. Fr. Mathias Wolff S.J., whose life and love for souls continue to inspire us.

sections.title: Becoming A JMJ Nun
sections.markdown:
Do you feel that God may be asking more of your life? Are you moved by the needs of the poor, and do you long to make a real difference? If your answer is yes, perhaps God is calling you to the Congregation of Jesus Mary Joseph.

## Who may enquire

We welcome young women who:

- practise their Catholic faith and take part in the liturgical and sacramental life of the Church;
- are open to sharing their own story of faith and life;
- wish to discern, with guidance, whether religious life is their path.

## How discernment begins

1. **Meet a vocation facilitator** — at least once a month, in person or online.
2. **Talk things through** — your story, your family and friends, your relationship with God, the Church, religious life, commitment and service.
3. **Pray and reflect** — with spiritual direction and a short or weekend retreat.
4. **Come to know JMJ** — our charism and history, and the life and vision of our Founder, Fr. Mathias Wolff S.J.
5. **Apply** — if discernment leads you forward, you complete the application and begin formation.

## The path of formation

Pre-candidacy and candidacy, a year of pre-novitiate, two years of novitiate, the juniorate under temporary vows, then perpetual profession — and lifelong ongoing formation. Read more on [Stages of Formation](/ministries/formation).

## Contact in the Hyderabad Province

**Sr. Bala Theresa Vatti**, Vocation Promoter — [blvatti75@gmail.com](mailto:blvatti75@gmail.com)
For Telangana, Andhra Pradesh (Kurnool district) and Madhya Pradesh.

You can also [write to the provincial office](/contact) or see [Whom To Contact?](/joining-us/whom-to-contact)

sections.title: Lay Association
sections.markdown:
The JMJ Association brings the Sisters of Jesus Mary Joseph and lay people together in one shared mission: to live the Gospel more fully and to respond to the suffering of others with practical compassion.

## Our aims

- To deepen each member's Christian calling and live Gospel values more fully.
- To show real, practical compassion for those who suffer.
- To bring different gifts together and find new ways of being merciful in today's world.

## Ways to take part

- **Through prayer and reflection** — supporting the ministries of JMJ by prayer, and in other ways where possible.
- **Through direct involvement** — taking part in our ministries as Associates and sharing in our spirituality and apostolic work.
- **Through projects** — giving a set period of service: mission experiences, work with the homeless, people struggling with addiction, migrants, survivors of trafficking or the underprivileged, care for creation, justice groups, peer ministry or homework clubs.

## What Associates commit to

- Regular prayer.
- Coming to know the JMJ charism through the Gospel and the lives of Fr. Mathias Wolff and Ven. Mary Glowrey.
- Promoting justice and compassion — at work or through a particular project.
- Taking part in regular meetings.
- Seeking, together with others, new merciful responses to the needs of today.

## Join us

In the Hyderabad Province, lay collaborators already work alongside the Sisters in our schools, hospitals and social service centres. To learn more or to become an Associate, please [contact the provincial office](/contact).

---

*Adapted from the Congregation of Jesus Mary Joseph website: [https://congregationjmj.org/lay-association](https://congregationjmj.org/lay-association).*

sections.title: Life of Ven. Mary Glowrey
sections.markdown:
**Venerable Mary of the Sacred Heart (Dr. Mary Glowrey), 1887 – 1957** — doctor, religious sister and medical missionary of the Society of Jesus Mary Joseph in India.

## Early life and medical studies

Mary Glowrey was born on **23 June 1887** at Birregurra, Victoria, Australia. A gifted student, she was among the first women to study medicine at the University of Melbourne, graduating in medicine and surgery in 1910 and later earning her Doctor of Medicine in 1919.

## A pioneering doctor

In 1911 she became the first woman resident doctor at Christchurch Hospital in New Zealand. Back in Melbourne she worked at several hospitals and, during the First World War, carried the workload of doctors who had gone to the front while running her own practice. In 1916 she became the first president of the Catholic Women's Social Guild.

## Called to India

Moved by the needs of women and children in India, she left Melbourne in January 1920 and arrived at **St. Joseph's Convent, Guntur, on 12 February 1920**. With special permission from Rome she became the first JMJ novice in India and made her first profession on **29 November 1921**, taking the name **Sr. Mary of the Sacred Heart**. With the permission of the Holy See she practised as a doctor while a religious — one of the first nun-doctor-missionaries.

## Healing ministry in Guntur

For some 36 years she served the sick in Guntur. The small dispensary she began grew into **St. Joseph's Hospital**, and she trained local women as nurses, midwives and compounders. In **1943** she founded the Catholic Hospitals' Association, today the **Catholic Health Association of India (CHAI)**, and was its first president.

## Last years and death

She remained faithful to God, to the sick and to the poor through long illness in her final years. She died in Bangalore on **5 May 1957**. People who had known her — in Guntur and far beyond — spoke at once of her holiness, humility and selfless service.

## Towards sainthood

Her cause for canonisation was opened and she was named a **Servant of God** in 2013. On **21 November 2025** the Church recognised her heroic virtues, and she is now honoured as **Venerable Mary Glowrey**.

Related pages: [Reflection on Mary Glowrey](/mary-glowrey/reflection) · [Prayers To Mary Glowrey](/mary-glowrey/prayers) · [Intercessions](/mary-glowrey/intercessions)

---

*Adapted from the Congregation of Jesus Mary Joseph website: [https://congregationjmj.org/life-of-ven-mary-glowrey](https://congregationjmj.org/life-of-ven-mary-glowrey).*

sections.title: Reflection on Mary Glowrey
sections.markdown:
Each month the Congregation publishes a reflection on the life and virtues of Ven. Mary Glowrey. Here are the themes of the most recent reflections.

## 2026

- **October — The woman who heard the cry of women in India.** A chain of providential encounters led Dr. Glowrey, the "Medical Apostle of India", to give her life to healing in India.
- **September — Fame of sanctity at the time of her death.** After 1957, the people of Guntur and many others spoke of her virtue, humility, zeal and devotion to her patients.
- **August — Fame of sanctity during her lifetime.** Long before the Church examined her virtues, those around her already saw her as a holy woman.
- **July — A life offered in love and sacrifice (1955–1957).** In illness and pain she stayed faithful to God, the sick and the poor.
- **May — A visionary in medical mission and women's empowerment (1946–1954).** At St. Joseph's Hospital her faith, skill and new ideas lifted up the women she trained and served.
- **April — A zealous and visionary medical missionary (1925–1946).** Selfless service, especially of poor families and women.
- **March — A vocation consecrated.** Entering religious life in 1920, she offered her medical gifts to God instead of laying them aside.
- **February — Arrival and missionary call.** Her arrival in Guntur in 1920 was a turning point for the JMJ mission in India.

## 2025

- **December — Foundations in a changing Melbourne (1901–1920).** The years in which she grew as a scholar, a doctor and a woman of faith.
- **October — The dawn of holiness (1887–1900).** The virtues of her childhood that later shaped her vocation.
- **September — Shaped by context, called by God.** The world she was born into, and how God called her within it.
- **August — Grace in action.** How her early life prepared her to touch thousands of poor and marginalised people.
- **June — A life rooted in virtue.** Reflecting on her 138th birthday, in the month of the Sacred Heart.
- **May — Her 68th "heavenly birthday".** Remembering her death as a witness to the Gospel lived out.

**[Read the full reflections on the Congregation website →](https://congregationjmj.org/mary-glowrey-inspirations)**

---

*Adapted from the Congregation of Jesus Mary Joseph website: [https://congregationjmj.org/mary-glowrey-inspirations](https://congregationjmj.org/mary-glowrey-inspirations).*

sections.title: Prayers To Mary Glowrey
sections.markdown:
We invite you to pray with us for the glorification of Ven. Mary Glowrey and to ask her intercession, especially for the sick and for all who care for them.

## Prayer of Sister Mary Glowrey

Her own prayer of self-surrender, asking God to fill and transform the one who prays.

## Prayer for her Cause

A prayer of thanksgiving for her consecrated life and her medical service in India, asking that, if it is God's will, her holiness be recognised by the Church.

## Prayer to Sr. Mary Glowrey

A prayer asking her intercession for a particular need, in trust and acceptance of God's will.

## Novena to Dr. Sr. Mary Glowrey

Nine days of prayer for healing and for health-care workers, for the unity of the Catholic Health Association of India, and for her canonisation. Each day ends with three *Hail Marys* and one *Glory Be*.

**[Read the full prayers on the Congregation website →](https://congregationjmj.org/prayers-to-mary-glowrey)**

Have you received a favour through her intercession? Please let us know through the [contact form](/contact) or share your intention on [Intercessions to Ven. Mary Glowrey](/mary-glowrey/intercessions).

---

*Adapted from the Congregation of Jesus Mary Joseph website: [https://congregationjmj.org/prayers-to-mary-glowrey](https://congregationjmj.org/prayers-to-mary-glowrey).*

sections.title: Intercessions to Ven. Mary Glowrey
sections.markdown:
Do you have a special intention — for healing, for a loved one, for your family or your work? You are welcome to entrust it to the intercession of Ven. Mary Glowrey. The Sisters will remember your intentions in their prayer.

## Send your prayer request

- **To the Congregation:** use the prayer request page on the Congregation website — **[Send a prayer request →](https://congregationjmj.org/drsr-mary-glowrey/prayer-request)**
- **To the Hyderabad Province:** write to us through our [contact form](/contact) with the subject *Prayer request*, or email [jmjhyd@gmail.com](mailto:jmjhyd@gmail.com).

## Favours received

If you believe you have received a grace or a healing through her intercession, please tell us. Such accounts are important for her cause.

## Pray with us

You can use the [Prayers To Mary Glowrey](/mary-glowrey/prayers), including the novena for the sick and for health-care workers.

---
